summary: Vacancy is still the biggest lever: the underwriting already counts the spring's occupancy (rent annualized from the last six months), and holding vacancy a point lower from there adds the most.

moves.title: Bring vacancy from 3.6% down to 2.6%
moves.impact: about $11,800 a year on the in-place NOI
moves.besideStory: Rent annualized from the last six months (occupancy gained in the spring)
moves.rationale: Vacancy loss ran $3,600 a month by June. One more point of occupancy on $1,177,500 of gross potential rent is about $11,800 a year; Safe already counts the spring's level, so the push is measured from there, less the management fee that rises with revenue.

moves.title: Re-bid snow removal and landscaping
moves.rationale: Contract services ran $32,500, with $14,000 of snow removal in four winter months. A seasonal contract with a cap would steady it.

moves.title: LED lighting in the common areas
moves.rationale: Electric runs $2,100 to $3,000 a month; LED common-area lighting usually trims about a tenth of that.
